old: If a recording stops unexpectedly: say, “The recording stopped and the session is over.” Open your eyes, name the location and day, press your feet or hands into a surface, move, look around, and use the five-step count. Don’t wait for the missing narrator to release you.
new: What if it’s a recording and it stops and you’re stuck? Say to yourself, “the recording has stopped, and the session is over” and then use the above method to force yourself out. Just opening your eyes and saying where you are, what day it is, pushing down with your feet or hands and moving about, looking around and then use the 5 step method. Don’t just sit there waiting for the voice to come back and release you.

old: Sleep is separate. A sleep recording may end in sleep or quiet rest. A waking recording shouldn’t end by preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, an undefined reset word, or an invitation to remain altered indefinitely.
new: NOTE: If you’re using a recording to go to sleep with, then it’s all right to have the recording put you to sleep or have you in a quiet resting state. However, if it’s for waking practice, it shouldn’t leave you in a role, with lowered judgement, with impaired movement capabilities, blank, with an undefined reset word, invited to stay altered indefinitely, etc.

old: Altered-state rule: do not ask for hidden truth while medically unsafe, panicking, sleep-deprived, nauseated, destabilized, manic, psychosis-like, or chemically overwhelmed. First stabilize. Truth that requires destabilization is not ready to be known directly. Ask for capacity, not content.

Sometimes it feels as though the subconscious knows something the conscious mind can’t yet tolerate. The subject may be sexuality, grief, trauma, family truth, betrayal, shame, vocation, relationship reality, illness fears, spiritual calling, addiction, identity, or moral conflict.
Interrogation is the dangerous response:
“Tell me now.” “Reveal everything.” “Stop hiding.” “I demand the truth.”

That pressure can produce flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, or a generally worse Tuesday. Flooding can make the adult capacities needed for pausing, comparing options, reality-testing, planning, and choosing much harder to reach. In that state, regulation and support come before deeper dialogue. Silence may be protection when the adult lacks enough regulation, support, humility, or practical capacity to receive the material.
Ask for the next tolerable piece:
“Do I need to know the content now, or do I need to build capacity first?”
“What would make the conscious mind 5% more able to receive this?”
“Can you show me the truth as a symbol, not a full revelation?”
“Can you give me the next protective action without revealing the whole story?”
“Who, if anyone, should help me hold this?”
A safer script:

“Wise subconscious, if there is something I cannot yet handle, please do not break it open violently. Help me become someone who can know it safely. Give me preparation before revelation. Give me grounding before memory. Give me support before intensity. Give me one next action.”

Hypnotic imagery can be meaningful without being literal. The mind symbolizes, compresses, distorts, dramatizes, and borrows from culture and fear. Around trauma and memory especially, treat an image as an image and involve outside support when needed.
new: NOTE: If it is medically unsafe or you are in a place of panic, sleep deprivation, nausea, deep destabilization, mania, psychosis like symptoms, feeling overwhelmed by chemicals etc. then first focus on stabilizing and then look for what your subconscious needs you to know! If it takes you destabilizing to know what your subconscious knows, it is not meant for you to know directly at this time! Focus on asking for capacity over content!

Sometimes, your subconscious knows something that your conscious self is not prepared to know. It may be something related to your sexuality, grief, trauma, family issues, betrayal, shame, vocation, a relationship, illness fears, spirituality, addiction, identity, moral issues etc.
What you DON’T want to do is bully your subconscious into telling you what it knows by saying things to yourself like:
“What is it you won’t tell me? What are you hiding? Tell me NOW! I am telling you to tell me!”

This often leads to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation etc. and can make your day SUCK! When you are flooded, you cannot access your adult capacities so focus on being able to regulate and getting support! Sometimes, it is better not to know what is not being said until your adult has the capacities to regulate, get support, be humble, etc. Just ask for what you need to know in a way that you CAN tolerate:

“What do I need to know that will help me get the capacity to know the thing you know that I need to know?” “What can you tell me, that will make my conscious self 5% better at knowing the thing you want to tell me?” “Can you tell me in symbolic form so I am not completely overwhelmed by the revelation?” “Can you tell me what I need to do to be safe, without actually telling me what it is”? “Do I need to know WHAT it is, or do I need to know that I need to get some support to have the capacity to know what it is, and who would be a good person to help me?” etc.
Instead, say to yourself something like this:

“Dear Wise Subconscious Mind, if there is something you know that my conscious self is not ready to know, please don’t break it open violently! Do what you can to make me able to know it in a way that is safe! Prepare me BEFORE you break it open! Ground me BEFORE you show me the memory! Support me BEFORE you make it intense!” etc.

REMEMBER: Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal, especially if it relates to trauma and memory. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!

old: Self-hypnosis can become very powerful during loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, sexual energy, prayer, sleep loss, or other plant-medicine-adjacent states. Sometimes the mind opens faster than the adult self can organize what is arriving.
new: Self hypnosis is powerful. Especially when you are in an altered state of consciousness, either through loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, sexual energy, prayer, not sleeping, or any other number of ways similar to plant medicines, often your mind opens faster then your adult can figure out what is going on.

old: Intensity then gets mistaken for meaning. Sometimes the inner child is finally speaking. Sometimes a Protector is showing fear, or shame, grief, anger, longing, and other buried material are asking for care. But an intense state can also be bodily overload, environmental chaos, sleep deprivation, or plain confusion. A frightening image isn’t automatically truth, a bad feeling isn’t automatically a lesson, and a “download” doesn’t deserve belief merely because it came with excellent lighting.
new: The problem is, that you THINK that because you are in an altered state that it MEANS something. Sometimes it is your inner child talking, but sometimes it is a Protector showing you their fear, sometimes it is your shame or your grief or your anger or your longing or whatever else is buried in you that wants to be taken care of, and sometimes it is just your body’s reaction to being overloaded, or chaos in your environment, or lack of sleep, or any number of other reasons for why what you are experiencing shouldn’t make sense. Just because you had a picture that scared you doesn’t mean that it is true. Just because you had a bad feeling doesn’t mean that it is a lesson you need to learn. Just because you had a download in nice lighting doesn’t mean that you should believe it.

old: Before trying to interpret the state, ask a simpler question:
new: What should you ask yourself first?

old: “What kind of problem is happening?”
new: “What kind of problem is happening?”

old: Start smaller:
new: Could you try this a bit smaller?

old: “Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”
new: Show me one body sensation, one word, whether to listen or rest today.

old: First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you’re trying to perform. Not experiencing an inner voice or image isn’t, by itself, resistance or a missing adult capacity. Correct an explicitly unwanted invitation. If you recognize a protective part, you can talk to it:
new: What in particular feels fake? If it's that you aren't getting an inner voice/image, it isn't necessarily a resistance or not being an adult. If it's telling you to do something you don't want to do, it's okay to correct it. If it turns out to be a protection, you can talk to it.

old: The fake feeling can also mean that a needed adult capacity isn’t available yet. Stop demanding a convincing voice. If you can already observe what is happening, borrow the particular warmth, boundary, or direction you lack. A real or imagined caring figure can help. Try one believable sentence or action and see how it is received.
new: It may be that you’re trying to access an adult part that isn’t there yet. If that’s the case, then stop trying to talk to an inner voice that you aren’t able to believe yet. If you have enough observing ego, borrow some from a real or imagined caring person. Try out some statements or actions etc. that you can believe, even if it’s just one sentence, and see how it goes.

old: There may be no answer, or the question may not help. You can change it, rest, or finish. If a concern about trust is actually present, ask:
“What do you need to know before you trust me?”
The reply may be extremely un-mystical: “Will you set the boundary?” “Will you keep the promise?” “Will you stop abandoning us?” “Will you stop substituting insight for action?”
new: There may not be an answer. There may not be an answer that will help you. You may need to try asking a different question or you may just need to rest or finish your inner work for the day. If you think it will be helpful, you can try asking your subconscious “What would you need to know in order to trust me?” Some examples of answers might be “I need to know you will set boundaries” “I need to know you will do what you said you will do” “I need to know you won’t keep leaving” “I need to know you won’t think that knowing something means that you don’t need to do anything about it” etc.

old: If a guard is recognizable, speak to it; otherwise stay with the feeling or preference that is actually present.
“You do not have to let me in. Just tell me what would make the doorway safer.”

If no clear child-state appears, use the session to notice one preference, curiosity, or beginner experiment instead of forcing an image. Identity-building and reparenting can happen in the same practice.
new: If you can figure out who the guard is, talk to it. If you can’t, just work with what you are aware of. You can say to the guard “You don’t have to let me in, just tell me what I need to do to make it safe”. Even if there isn’t a child part that you can talk to, you can work with whatever you are aware of. You can work on your preferences or something that you’re curious about or something that you’re willing to try as a beginner etc. and see how it goes. Work on developing a sense of who you are and reparent yourself as best you can.

old: Notice whether the anxiety is manageable and you want to stay with it, or whether you need less contact. When it is escalating or overwhelming, stop searching for content and help the body first.
Feet. Chair. Breath. Room.

“Little one, I am here. Protector, thank you for warning me. You do not have to scream for me to listen. If there is real action needed, show me one step. If there is no action needed, help the body stand down gently.”

Get professional help when anxiety includes chest pain, fainting, suicidal thoughts, psychosis-like or mania-like symptoms, severe dissociation, inability to sleep, or urges to harm yourself or someone else. Appendix D has the longer anxiety toolbox.
new: Find out if the anxiety is bad enough that you want to decrease contact with it or if you can manage it and let it continue. If the anxiety is getting too bad, then you need to help your body, like the following:
-Where are your feet? Where are you sitting? Focus on your body and your breathing.

-Tell your Little parts and Protector parts that you’re there for your Little parts and that you recognize that your Protector parts are trying to protect you and that you don’t need them to scream at you in order for you to know that something is wrong. Ask them if they need you to do something and if they do, ask them to show you one step at a time that you can do. If they don’t, then ask them to let your body calm down.

If you’re having chest pain, fainting, suicidal thoughts, psychosis-like symptoms, mania-like symptoms, severe dissociative symptoms, not being able to sleep, wanting to hurt yourself or somebody else, etc. then you need to get help. For more on handling anxiety, see the toolbox in Appendix D.

old: Open your eyes. Move. Touch something textured. Name five objects. End the deeper practice for the day.
new: Open your eyes, move around, feel something, name 5 things that you can see, and end your work for the day.

old: Return to food, sleep, chores, humility, and somebody who will disagree with you.
“If this insight is real, it will survive sleep, food, time, humility, and feedback.”
new: Go eat, go to sleep, do some chores, accept some humility, find somebody to disagree with you, etc.
What do you say to yourself in that moment? “If it’s really there, it’ll still be here after a good night’s sleep, some food, some time, etc, and some subsequent humility, feedback, etc, etc.”

old: When the practice turns into a technical performance, stop improving it. Put one hand on the heart and one on the solar plexus.
“I am not here to do this perfectly. I am here to be in relationship with what is deeper than my surface mind.”
“What would make this feel more like communion and less like performance?”
Silence may be the answer. Rest may be the answer. One honest action may be the answer. Take the answer that actually arrived.
new: You’re being too analytical. “What if you didn’t try?” Put your hand on your heart, your other on your solar plexis, and say, “I don’t have to do this. I’m here for a relationship with something deeper than my surface mind.” “What can you do to make this a communion, not a performance?” Then do something. Usually it’s silence, resting, or doing something. Whatever it is, just do it.

old: Ask the bliss to become specific.
“What task, boundary, meal, rest, repair, or conversation does love require next?”
new: You’re being too blissful, diffuse, etc. Bring it down to a more specific level. “What’s the smallest, most specific thing you can do to demonstrate the love you’re feeling?”

old: Don’t pry.
“Show me the capacity before the content.”
new: You’re wanting to know something you’re not supposed to know yet. Refrain from doing anything, and say, “Show me more capacity first, and if what I want to know is really for me, you’ll show me later on.”

old: Sit up and open your eyes.
“What real action is this fantasy replacing?”
new: You’re daydreaming. Sit up and open your eyes, and ask yourself, “What are you avoiding doing in the real world by doing this?”

old: “Where has divine love not yet descended into the wound?”

A genuine opening can show you a depth of love or freedom you hadn’t known was possible. Let that matter without demanding the child receive it on command. Prayer can also evoke abandonment or condemnation, or a teacher’s betrayal can damage something sacred. Ask what was lost and what needs questioning; more of the same practice isn’t automatically the answer.

Sometimes practical care helps while the available horizon of life still feels too small. Curiosity about deeper happiness is worth following without pretending to believe an explanation. Other people already have enough love and meaning for the life they want. Spirituality doesn’t need to become another assignment.
new: You’re doing spiritual bypass. Ask yourself, “Where has divine love not come down and hugged your hurt yet?”

You’ve had some amazing opening that showed you how much more love and freedom is possible, but your kid isn’t receiving it. Or maybe prayer has led you to feel abandoned or condemned by God. Or maybe a teacher betrayed you. Whatever the problem, it’s not going to get resolved by doing more of the same.

Sometimes you just need to do something practical to take care of yourself until the horizon of your life expands enough for what you’re seeking to enter. Or you need to follow your curiosity for what will make you happy, regardless of whether it makes sense or not. Or you need to realize you already have plenty of love and meaning in your life, and this whole spirituality thing is optional.

old: A real wound and a checking loop can coexist. Ask whether this round helps you feel, understand, decide, or respond differently—or whether you’re checking the same question for reassurance. Grief and practice can revisit familiar ground; novelty isn’t required every time.

When it is a checking loop, let the thought remain without arguing with it or chasing it away, and return to a chosen activity or relationship. You don’t have to hold an inner meeting every time a thought appears or complete a ritual before you’re allowed to live.
“What direction would the Leader choose now?”
new: You’re processing the same stuff over and over again. First ask yourself, “Do I really have something I need to deal with, or am I just doing a check?” It’s okay to go over the same stuff over and over again (especially when you’re grieving or doing a practice), but sometimes you’re just doing a check.
If you determine you’re doing a check, say to yourself, “It’s okay for that thought to be there, but I don’t need to hold a meeting with it right now. I’m going to do ____ instead.”
Ask yourself, “What would your Leader do in this situation?”

old: “What would prove to the inner child that the adult is real?”
Then do the thing.
new: You’re doing hypnosis over and over again without making changes in your life. Ask yourself, “What can I do to show my kid I’m for real?” Then go do it.

old: The subconscious isn’t an AI model, but prompt engineering offers one useful lesson: the shape of a question changes what kind of answer can appear. A prompt should make you more present, honest, loving, and able to hear the next signal—never more controlling.
I use seven elements when I want a prompt to be precise:
Role: who or what you are addressing.
Context: what situation you are bringing.
Intention: what kind of change is desired.
Constraint: safety, truth, kindness, no forcing, no false certainty, and capacity before content.
Output: image, phrase, body signal, memory, next action, question, symbol, silence, or rest.
Evaluation: true, kind, timely, stabilizing, specific, testable.
Iteration: revise after life gives feedback.
Always include a safe fallback so the analytical mind doesn’t treat silence as failure and manufacture an answer.

“And if the system needs more time to process this, or if silence is the safest answer today, let my body settle into deeper comfortable rest instead. A peaceful silence is a fully successful answer.”
Sometimes nothing answers because nothing is happening. Sometimes the answer is not yet, rest first, build capacity, or do the ordinary thing you already know to do.
new: Your subconscious mind is NOT a large language model of AI. However, there is a bit of overlap in the way you can ask questions to both. So, if you know how to do prompt engineering for AI, this can be very useful to use it to help you be more present, honest, loving etc. On the other hand, if you use it to be more controlling, it will NOT work.
To get as much precision as possible, you need to include the following in your prompt:
Role: Who or what are you talking to?
Context: Give some context so it knows what you’re talking about.
Intention: What do you want to change or accomplish?
Constraint: What do you need to do to make sure your asking is safe, true, kind etc.
Output: How do you want to receive the answer? As an image, phrase, sensation in your body, memory, action, question, symbol, silence, rest etc.
Evaluation: How are you going to evaluate the answer? How will you know if it’s true, kind, timely, stabilizing, specific, testable etc?
Iteration: Iterate by changing your prompt depending on what you get from reality as feedback.

Most importantly, you always need to make your prompt “safe” otherwise, the analytical part of your mind will “make up” an answer just so it fits with your prompt. I usually add the following to my prompt:

“If you need more time or the best and safest answer is silence, then I ask you to make my body go into a deeper state of comfortable rest. A peaceful silence would be a successful answer to my question.”
There is a very good chance there is no answer for your question because there is nothing happening. It might be that it’s not time yet, or that you need to go rest or do whatever you need to do.
Once you do that, here are the core prompts you can use:

old: For clarity:

“Wise subconscious, please show me what is true, kind, and timely. If the full truth of this situation is too intense for my body to integrate today, pass it to my conscious mind only as a gentle symbol, a body signal, or a single next step. Show me my capacity to hold peace before you show me the content of the wound.”
For resistance:
“What are you protecting me from, and what would help you trust me 1% more?”
For the inner child:
“Little one, what do you need me to understand, and what can I do today so you are not alone with it?”
For the Protector:
“What real-world action would make this system safer?”
For the Leader/Guru:
“What direction serves truth, love, life, and the benefit of all beings?”
For intuition:
“Let intuition offer a signal, let analysis examine its meaning, let the body give feedback, and let reality test the interpretation.”
For separating intuition from conditioning:

“Wise subconscious, please help me look at this impulse clearly. If part of this signal belongs to family programming, religious fear, marketing, erotic imprinting, political tribe, trauma response, or a childhood bargain for belonging, let that part become visible as conditioning. Let it soften or step back only as much as is safe. Leave behind whatever belongs to true guidance, the universal heart, and a better ordinary life. Let my body feel the difference.”
For daydreaming:
“If this daydream is useful, reveal the guidance inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and help me deal with what I need to deal with.”
For anxiety:
“What is anxiety trying to protect, and what would help it trust the adult self?”
For hidden truth:
“If the full truth would overwhelm me, please do not reveal it all. Show me the capacity before the content.”
For integration:
“What ordinary-life action would prove that I heard correctly?”
The prompt defines the search. NLP language affects how gently the question enters. Used together, they can create a safer field for an answer without pretending the answer is automatically true.
new: For getting clarity: “I ask you, my wise subconscious mind, to show me what is true, kind and timely. If what you want to show me is too intense for me to integrate, please transfer it to my conscious mind in a way I can integrate it, for instance as a symbol, a signal in my body, a next step I can take. Most importantly, show me first my capacity to be peaceful, and then, the content of my wounding.”
When you experience resistance: “What are you protecting me from? How can you trust me 1% more?”
When you want to ask your inner child something: “What do you want me to know? What do you need me to do today so that you are not alone in dealing with it?”
When you want to ask one of your protectors something: “What do you need me to do in the external world so that you can feel that you and the system are safe?”
When you want to ask your leader or guru self: “What direction is the most in alignment with truth, love, life and all beings?”

When you want to listen to your intuition: “I ask my intuition to give me a signal, my analytical mind to decipher it, my body to give me feedback as to whether my deciphering is correct and reality to give me feedback as to whether my deciphering is correct.”

When you want to know if a particular intuition you have is coming from your universal heart or from your programming (this one is longer and more complicated): “I ask my wise subconscious mind to help me see if the intuition or impulse I have about …is coming from my universal heart or from my family, my religion, marketing, erotic programming, my political tribe, my trauma response or an old deal I did as a child to belong. If it’s coming from my programming, I ask the parts responsible for it to step back and soften so that I can have true guidance from my universal heart that will help me make my life better in the most simple ways possible. Let my body give me feedback as to the difference.”

When you are daydreaming: “If this daydream has useful guidance for me, I ask my wise subconscious mind to show it to me. If this is my way of not dealing with my life, I ask my wise subconscious mind to help me come back to the present and deal with my life.”
When you are anxious: “What are you protecting me from? How can you trust more my adult self?”

When you suspect there is something true that you don’t know: “If knowing the truth is too much for me, please don’t show me everything. Show me first my capacity to be peaceful, and then, the content of my wounding.”
Once you get an answer, you can ask: “What can I do in my ordinary life to integrate what I have heard?”
The prompt will tell your subconscious what you want. The NLP will make sure you are getting it in a safe way.

old: Gather attention, notice what is here, offer one fitting response, wait, then come all the way back. You can meet a difficulty or develop love, curiosity, play, or confidence. Nothing dramatic has to happen.
new: To work on difficulties or cultivate positive qualities (love, curiosity, play, confidence, etc.), simply gather attention and do these steps, in order: 1) Attention; 2) Notice; 3) Respond; 4) Wait; 5) Come all the way back . Not much needs to happen in each session!

old: Before the first session, read the induction and full return below while awake. Set aside time somewhere physically secure. Choose one purpose and what you are leaving alone today. Then put the screen aside; the practice is something you learn to conduct, not a checklist to keep reading.
new: It may be helpful, prior to your first session, to read through the induction and the full return in waking life, so you’re more familiar with it. Give yourself a chunk of time when you can be physically secure for the time it takes. Prior to each session, consider what one thing you’re going to be working on or cultivating during this session, and what you’re going to leave alone. Put this screen on the shelf and conduct the practice.

old: Conscious agreement is one thing. Unconscious receptivity is another. Emotional compliance is another. Legal and ethical consent is another. A mind can be influenced without the adult self having clearly chosen the influence.
new: Is a conscious agreement the same as being unconsciously receptive, emotionally compliant or legally and ethically consenting? What if someone influences a persons mind other then when they are a legal adult?

old: A line associated with the Silva Mind Control tradition says it plainly:
new: From the school of Silva Mind Control:

old: Advertising, fear, craving, screens, tribe, resentment, authority, loneliness, and repetition are already training the mind. Self-hypnosis lets you practice from inside it: befriending the deeper layers, listening closely, and making adult choice more available.
new: You are surrounded by many forces who are already using these techniques to train your mind. Wouldn’t it be great if you could turn the tables around and use them yourself? When you learn to use these techniques on yourself, you are using self-hypnosis techniques to befriend your deeper mind, listen to it, and empower yourself to make more of your own choices as an adult.
